title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual sexually explicit images of a real person. The system itself had no safeguards that prevented this use. The deployer of the technology, whoever created or hosted the tool, did not restrict generation of images of real identifiable people or flag when a user requested this capability.

The failure happened at the point of use. A person obtained photos of a woman from her private social media and used an AI tool to create obscene manipulated images, then distributed them across multiple platforms under false identities. No detection system on the platforms where the images were shared caught and removed the content before the victim discovered it was being distributed.

It is not established whether the AI system's terms of service prohibited this use, whether any detection occurred, or what technical measures might have prevented the initial generation or distribution of the images.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and distributing artificial intelligence-generated obscene images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering, obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used AI technology to create morphed explicit images. He then circulated this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The case began when the 22-year-old victim reported to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi that she had received messages informing her that her manipulated photographs and videos were being shared across Discord servers and fake Instagram accounts. During their investigation, police analyzed digital footprints and traced the fake profiles back to Bansal. He admitted during interrogation that he knew the woman from college and had developed personal resentment toward her after repeated arguments. Police recovered a mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence connected to the crime, and further investigation is continuing.
